title: Mali's king is in Cairo
body: Mansa Musa, the king of Mali, is in Cairo on a pilgrimage, a holy journey to Mecca. His huge company is buying and selling in the markets. Jamil offers you a share in his cloth sales to them.

choices.label: Put money into Jamil's cloth
choices.hint: He sells to the Malians. You share the profit.

choices.label: Buy two chests of gold now
choices.hint: Jamil's friend sells a chest for 90, a little under the 100 the market asks. Two chests are a venture on one price, so the sum is large.

choices.label: Watch from the street
choices.hint: Your partners like a steady house.

note: Al-Umari wrote that the people of Cairo made great profits from the Malians, and that the price of gold fell.

sources.at: pp. 269 to 273; al-Umari on the Malians in Cairo

title: The canal is filling
body: The Nile flood is filling the canal to Alexandria. Kamil owns a boat that sails with the flood, and he has room for goods. The sugar buyers at Alexandria are waiting.

choices.label: Buy four loads of sugar and ship them
choices.hint: Four loads cost 220 dinars, and the boat brings back 230 in two seasons. The first boats sell first, and other owners will grumble.

note: Al-Maqrizi wrote that ships loaded with crops, spices and sugar set sail when the Nile filled the Alexandria canal. That was from 25 July to 23 August.

sources.at: p. 150; al-Maqrizi on the Alexandria canal and the flood

title: Another market, a better price
body: Zubayda sells linen in another part of Cairo. She says shops there get more for linen than yours do. She offers to sell your next cloth in her market for a fee.

choices.label: Sell in her market
choices.hint: Her fee is high. Your neighbours will see you go.

choices.label: Stay in your own market
choices.hint: No fee, and your neighbours are glad.

note: Al-Maqrizi counted 54 markets in Cairo. Shops that sold the same goods stood together, which saved buyers time and the cost of carrying goods.

sources.at: Introduction n. 11, and Background n. 24; the count of markets, and shops of one trade standing together

title: Bread is dear
body: Bread is still dear in Cairo. Grain comes up from Syria and Palestine, and buyers crowd the markets. Bilal needs carts for the grain roads, and he asks if the house will lend two.

choices.label: Lend two carts for a fee
choices.hint: You earn 5 dinars. The street will talk, and the officers will remember.

choices.label: Give bread money to your street
choices.hint: It costs 5 dinars. Your neighbours will remember.

choices.label: Keep your carts for your own goods

note: In 1336 Cairo had one of its ten big food shortages. The sultan ordered grain to be brought in from Syria and Palestine. A historian of Cairo's grain prices reports this.

sources.at: p. 198 and note 8; the sultan's order of 1336, which he takes from Shoshan 1993, p. 61

title: Another house asks about Yusuf
body: A friend warns you. The Mansur house is asking what you pay Yusuf. A big house can offer more than a small one. Yusuf has said nothing to you about it.

choices.label: Ask Yusuf if he is content
choices.hint: It costs 4 dinars for the visit. He will tell you the truth.

choices.label: Raise his pay a little and tell him why
choices.hint: It costs 5 dinars. Other agents will hear of it.

choices.label: Say nothing and watch
choices.hint: It costs nothing now. Partners like a steady house, though Yusuf may feel unseen.

note: A big Jewish merchant house of the 1020s and 1030s traded flax. It is said to have used a whole army of Jewish and Muslim agents. Two scholars report this from an earlier historian, Norman Stillman.

sources.at: p. 17; the whole army of agents, from Stillman, as they report it
